Data leakage!
In statistics and machine learning,
leakage (also known as data leakage or target leakage)
is the use of information in the model training process
which would not be expected to be available at prediction time,
causing the predictive scores (metrics) to overestimate the model's utility when
run in a production environment.
Leakage is often subtle and indirect, making it hard to detect and eliminate.
Examples:
WOE calculation before train-test split
Variable ‘Exit-talk’ in HR turnover prediction dataset
Extreme case: including the class label as a variable
